label: Claude Fable 5.2
output:
Here's a draft you can post as is:

---

D. Bergeron, you asked for a straight answer before the 4th, and you are right to ask. Here it is: we are not closing and we are not moving. It is the opposite. I bought the building.

I wanted to keep this as a surprise for the reopening. I imagined telling you all on the day, with the new oven behind me. But my nephew showed me this thread and I think the surprise is finished, so I will tell you everything now.

First the carnets, because that is the question that matters most to the people who paid. We sold 214 carnets in October, $60 for 12 loaves. All of them are still good. There is no expiry date. noodle_and_crumb, your 7 loaves are safe, and they will come out of a brand new oven. On top of that, every carnet holder gets one free croissant in January, after we reopen. And if somebody really wants their money back, come see me at the bakery and I will give it back. No questions, no hard feelings.

Now the building. Marc-Antoine, your cousin is half right. The building at the corner was sold, the ground floor and the three apartments. It was sold to me. The owner, M. Ferland, is 81 years old and he is retiring to Sherbrooke with his daughter. He offered it to me before anybody else, and we signed at the notary on December 15. This is a man who has come in every morning for 17 years for his baguette pas trop cuite. He cried a little at the notary, and I was not much better. So no condos, no bank, no vape shop. What you describe is what usually happens around here, we have all seen it. This time it went the other way, and it means nobody can decide to put something else in that corner. The bakery stays as long as I can lift a tray.

For the tenants upstairs, and for everybody who worried about them: the three apartments stay rented. Same tenants, same rent. I promised it to them in writing, and I am saying it here too, in front of the whole neighbourhood.

About the sign. My nephew Thomas wrote it at 6 in the morning, and "Grande nouvelle bientôt!" was his idea. I said ok without thinking. When I read it again after seeing this thread, I understood the problem. A closed door and a mystery is not a good mix on this street. That one is on me. Thomas only wanted to help.

And the half-empty shelves this morning, jules_on_waverly: we sold everything for Christmas Eve. 400 bûches. It has nothing to do with closing. Your pain de campagne is not going anywhere.

So why are we closed from January 4 to 18? For the work. Two things are happening.

One, a new oven. It is a deck oven with 4 decks, coming from a supplier in Laval. The old one is from 1998 and it broke down 3 times this year. It gave what it could.

Two, we are taking the space at the back, the old storage room of the dépanneur. There will be 6 small tables. After 17 years, finally you can sit down.

I also want to say one thing, and I don't say it to start a fight. I understand why people worry. Mile End has lost many small shops, and when you see a sign taped on a door you think the worst. In your place I would probably think the same. D. Bergeron, your question was fair and you asked it politely. But seeing the word scam next to the name of my bakery, that hurt. I will not pretend it didn't. We opened in March 2009. Seventeen years on this street. I would not take $60 from my neighbours and then lock the door. I hope after today nobody has to wonder about that.

Priya, thank you. I read what you wrote about the Saturday chocolatines and it did me good on a hard day. Thank you also to everybody else who defended us here. I saw it and I will not forget it.

The dates, so nobody has to search:

Closed January 4 to 18 for the work.

Reopening Tuesday, January 19, at 7 in the morning.

Saturday, January 23, the real celebration. Everybody is invited, carnet or no carnet, regular or not. Coffee and a piece of the new bread, free. Come see the oven, come try the tables, come say hello. If you were worried this week, come especially.

In a way this thread shows me that people care about the place, and I take that as a compliment, even if my heart jumped a little when I read it. Thank you for caring this much about a bakery.

À bientôt,
Hélène Gagnon
Boulangerie Le Pétrin Doré

---

I gave the 7 a.m. time for Tuesday the 19th, but you didn't give me an hour for Saturday the 23rd, so the post only gives the date. If the celebration starts at a set time, add it to that line.
